How does selling a house work across Wisconsin's 72 counties?

Selling in Wisconsin means dealing with county offices more than state ones. The state has 72 counties, and each one runs its own register of deeds, treasurer and clerk, all elected officials. Milwaukee County is the largest at 924,216 people in the 2025 Census estimate, while Menominee County is the smallest at 4,199.

That spread matters when you sell. A deed recorded in Milwaukee goes to a busy office with its own procedures. A deed recorded in a northern county may go through a much smaller counter. The rules in the statutes are the same, but timing and paperwork habits differ. Our guides for recording a deed in Wisconsin and Wisconsin by city and county sort out who to call.

What does a seller pay at closing in Wisconsin?

The biggest statutory cost is the real estate transfer fee. State law puts it on the grantor, meaning the seller, at 30 cents for each $100 of value or fraction of $100. The register of deeds collects it when the deed is submitted for recording.

The deed itself carries a separate $30 recording fee under the statute that sets register of deeds charges. For land contracts, the value used for the transfer fee is the total principal the buyer agrees to pay. The return that goes with the deed must be signed by both seller and buyer.

  • Transfer fee: 30 cents per $100 of value, paid by the seller.
  • Recording fee: $30 for a deed.
  • Property tax: unpaid balances and the current year's share usually get settled at closing.
  • Payoffs: any mortgage or lien against the property.

Our Wisconsin seller closing costs guide walks through the line items, and the quitclaim deed guide covers a simpler transfer between family members.

What disclosure does a Wisconsin seller owe the buyer?

Most sellers must hand the buyer a real estate condition report. The owner has to furnish it no later than 10 days after the contract of sale is accepted. The duty applies to sales, exchanges and land contracts unless the transfer is exempt from the transfer fee.

There is an exception for people who have never lived in the property and act as a personal representative, trustee, conservator or court supervised fiduciary. That is common with inherited houses, where the person selling is the estate's representative and never occupied the home.

Disclosure is where a cash sale often feels lighter. When a buyer purchases as-is, the conversation is about what the house is, not about negotiating repairs after an inspection. You still complete the paperwork the statute asks for. If you are unsure whether you are exempt, ask the closing attorney or title company before signing.

How do property taxes work when you sell in Wisconsin?

Property tax is set locally and collected through the county system. Real property taxes are due in full by January 31, or in two equal installments, the first by January 31 and the second by July 31.

Tax questions on a particular parcel go to the treasurer in the county or municipality where the house sits, so ask that office for the exact amount due before closing. Our Wisconsin property tax guide lays out appeals and exemptions, and these local pages cover the counties people ask about most:

  • Milwaukee County property tax guide
  • Dane County property tax guide
  • Waukesha County property tax guide
  • Brown County property tax guide

If taxes are far behind, talk to the treasurer early. Selling before the problem grows keeps more control in your hands.

How does foreclosure work in Wisconsin?

Wisconsin mortgage foreclosure goes through the courts, and owners get real time. For an owner occupied one to four family home, a sale generally cannot happen until six months after judgment if the mortgage was signed on or after April 27, 2016. For older mortgages the wait is 12 months.

The first printing of the sale notice cannot come sooner than four months after judgment under the newer rule. If the owner asks the court before judgment and shows a good faith effort to sell, with a listing agreement signed, the wait can stretch to eight months.

Mortgage signedEarliest sheriff sale after judgment
Before April 27, 201612 months
On or after April 27, 20166 months
On or after April 27, 2016, owner listing with a broker8 months on court motion

These periods apply to the types of property described in the statute and have exceptions, so confirm yours with a Wisconsin attorney. A direct sale during this window can pay off the lender and let you walk away with whatever equity remains.

What happens when you sell an inherited house in Wisconsin?

It depends on how the house was owned and how large the estate is. When the property subject to administration does not exceed $50,000 in gross value, an heir, the trustee of a revocable trust, the person named in the will, or a guardian can collect and transfer property by affidavit instead of opening a full probate.

  • Check how the deed reads: joint tenancy, life estate and transfer on death deeds change the steps.
  • Ask the probate court clerk in the county where the person lived about forms and filing.
  • Expect the register of deeds to want the recorded deed and legal description.

More detail is in our guides to the probate process, transfer on death deeds and estate and inheritance tax.

Can you sell a Wisconsin house that has tenants?

Yes, but notices and timing drive the plan. For a month to month or week to week tenant who has not paid rent, a landlord can give a notice to pay or vacate on a date at least five days after the notice. A separate 14 day notice to vacate can end a month to month tenancy while the tenant is in default.

Check the lease and the notice dates before you set a closing, because a tenant's status can change what a buyer will accept. Read more in our eviction notice guide, the landlord and tenant guide and the page on squatters and adverse possession.

How does Wisconsin's homestead protection affect a sale?

The homestead exemption protects a resident owner's occupied home from creditors up to $75,000. It does not reach mortgages, mechanics' liens, purchase money liens or taxes. The protection continues for up to $75,000 of sale proceeds for two years if you intend to buy another homestead with them.

Our Wisconsin homestead exemption guide covers it in more depth.

What does an as-is cash sale look like, and what should you check in Wisconsin?

An as-is cash sale means the buyer takes the house in its present condition and does not ask you to fix it. That suits houses with deferred maintenance, tenant trouble, estate delays or looming foreclosure. You still sign a deed, complete the transfer return and pay the transfer fee.

Wisconsin has one health related item worth testing for. The state health department says about one in ten Wisconsin homes has high radon levels, and a test kit costs $10 to $30. Radon is a reason buyers sometimes ask for a test, so knowing your number first removes a surprise.

  • Gather the deed, the latest tax bill and any mortgage statement.
  • Find out who the county register of deeds and treasurer are for the parcel.
  • Ask a title company or attorney how they handle closings in your county.
  • Confirm any estate or tenant documents before you list a date.

Prices and timelines vary by property, so we do not quote either here. Tell us about the house and we will take it from there.

Frequently asked questions

How many counties does Wisconsin have?

Wisconsin has 72 counties. Each runs its own register of deeds and treasurer, so recording and tax questions go to the county where the house sits.

Who pays the transfer fee when selling a house in Wisconsin?

The seller pays. The fee is 30 cents for each $100 of value and the register of deeds collects it when the deed is recorded.

Is foreclosure in Wisconsin handled by a court?

Yes. A court enters judgment first. For many owner occupied homes the sheriff sale cannot happen until six or twelve months after judgment, depending on when the mortgage was signed.

When are Wisconsin property taxes due?

Real property taxes are due in full by January 31 or in two equal payments, the first by January 31 and the second by July 31.

Do I need to disclose problems to a Wisconsin buyer?

Most sellers must deliver a real estate condition report within 10 days after a contract is accepted. Personal representatives and some other fiduciaries who never lived in the home are excused.

Can I sell a house in Wisconsin without making repairs?

Yes. In an as-is sale the buyer accepts the house in its present condition. You still complete the deed, the transfer return and any required disclosure.
